newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $67, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $67, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle early Thursday were bid $67.00 per cwt but bids were passed by owners pricing cattle at $69.00 to $70.00, feedlot sources said.

The bids were $2.00 lower than prices paid in the bulk of this week's active sales at $69.00. The lower bids early Thursday reflected CME live cattle futures limit-down close Wednesday, sources noted.
However, most of this week's showlists in Kansas and the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma area were close to being depleted before futures collapsed, sources said.
"We'll just wait and see what happens the next few days before seeing where prices will go next," a Kansas source said.
Cash cattle prices earlier this week were elevated by a sharp jump in beef values since April 9, sources said.

However, cattle futures collapsed Wednesday on wire service reports a man in Indiana had died in March of the rare brain disease Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD). The disease kills about 250 people a year in the U.S. but has not been linked to any particular source.

British scientists last year identified a strain of CJD as possibly linked to the deadly cattle disease Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE). BSE has never been found in U.S. cattle and U.S. CJD cases were not the same strain as in England.
